decisions.reason: As a core upholstery fabric with continued market presence, it draws directly on the firm's existing upholstery know-how and can be incrementally refined through customer feedback and in-house development rather than withdrawn.

This decorative fabric remains close to the firm's established design and weaving capabilities, but its lighter prominence suggests a somewhat higher pruning risk if learning from demand stays only moderate.

The flame-retardant curtain fabric fits the firm's strong contract and functional-textile knowledge base especially well, so absorptive capacity and likely ongoing refinement make withdrawal unlikely.

The double-face wool-blend fabric builds on familiar decorative-textile competences, yet its more niche material profile and lower visibility leave a moderate chance of rationalisation if it does not justify collection space.

As a newly launched structured fabric spanning upholstery and curtains, it is closely related to the firm's broad existing offer and dedicated presentation suggests the firm expects to learn and improve it rather than exit quickly.
